name: Forehand drive
summary: A short, compact topspin hit on your forehand side. The first attacking stroke to learn.
whenToUse: Against a topspin or no-spin ball that bounces up to your forehand side at a comfortable height. It's your bread-and-butter rally shot.

keyPoints.stance: Feet a little wider than shoulders, right foot slightly back (left foot if left-handed), knees bent.
keyPoints.bodyAction: Turn your waist and shoulders back as the ball comes, then turn forward into the ball. Weight moves from your back foot to your front foot.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Compact. The bat starts at about waist height beside you and finishes in front of your forehead.
keyPoints.timing: Contact at the top of the bounce, slightly in front of your body.
keyPoints.tablePosition: About half a metre to a metre from the end line.
keyPoints.freeArm: Up in front of you. It helps you turn and keeps you balanced.
keyPoints.batArm: Elbow relaxed and a little away from your body, about a right angle. The forearm drives forward and slightly up; bat face slightly closed.
keyPoints.recovery: Let the bat finish, then bring it straight back to ready in front of you.
keyPoints.anticipation: Watch your opponent's bat. A topspin coming at you needs a slightly closed bat; a flatter ball needs a slightly more open one.

cues: Top of the bounce, in front

learningPath.task: Watch the 3D player at slow speed. Step through each phase: ready, backswing, contact, follow-through, recover.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues without looking.

learningPath.task: Follow-along mode: copy the player without a ball, slow and exact, then at normal speed.
learningPath.passCheck: 3 sets of 10, then yes to all three self-checks.
selfChecks: Did your waist turn back before the swing?
Did the bat finish in front of your forehead?
Did you come back to ready each time?

learningPath.task: First contact with slow, regular balls to one spot. Just hit the table, any depth.
learningPath.passCheck: 7 of 10 on the table with the right shape.

learningPath.task: Build a run: forehand cross-court until 20 in a row, then aim for the last third of the table.
learningPath.passCheck: 20 in a row, then 10 of 20 deep.

learningPath.task: Combine it: push, then drive when the ball comes long. Then side-step between two points.
learningPath.passCheck: 7 of 10 patterns with both shots on the table.

learningPath.task: Play the push-and-drive game. Choose the drive only when the ball is long or high.
learningPath.passCheck: Win 3 points with your forehand drive.

learningPath.task: Test: forehand drives in a row.

gamePatterns.situation: Your opponent's push comes long or a bit high to your forehand.
gamePatterns.how: It is still backspin: open the bat slightly, lift more than a normal drive and aim deep to their backhand. If the push is low, loop it instead.

gamePatterns.situation: A forehand rally, corner to corner.
gamePatterns.how: Keep it cross-court and deep. When a ball lands short or high, change direction down the line.

troubleshooting.symptom: The ball goes into the net
causes: Contact too late, when the ball is falling
fixes: Hit at the top of the bounce, in front of you
Swing more forward, finish at your forehead not above your head

causes: Too close to or too far from the table
fixes: Move your feet first, then swing
Find an arm's length from the ball at contact

causes: Weight stays on the front foot
fixes: Turn back as the ball comes
Feel the weight move from back foot to front foot

penholdNotes: Same body action. Keep the wrist a little firmer; the penhold grip makes it easy to over-use the wrist.
